title: On the Performance of Randomly Generated Codebooks in Near-Field Communications
summary: Near-field communication with large antenna arrays requires beamforming techniques that account for spherical wavefront effects. While predefined codebooks are widely used in multiple-antenna wireless systems, the performance of randomly generated codebooks in the near-field region has not been investigated. In this work, we study four randomly generated codebooks for near-field communications: random vector quantization (RVQ), random phase (RP), random far-field (RFF), and random near-field (RNF) codebooks. We use the known RVQ gain distribution as a benchmark. For RP, we derive a large-array bulk approximation and characterize the high-gain tail behavior of the gain distribution. For RNF, we characterize the high-gain tail behavior of the gain distribution. For RFF, we derive an analytical approximation for the maximum achievable beamforming gain when far-field beams are used to serve near-field users, along with the corresponding maximizing far-field direction. We also analyze the maximum-gain scaling with codebook size. Monte Carlo simulations verify the analytical results and show that RVQ and RP degrade significantly as the array size increases, while RNF achieves the most favorable high-gain scaling. RFF can outperform RVQ and RP for finite codebook sizes, but its maximum gain saturates below one due to the phase mismatch between the far-field beams and the near-field channel. These results show how codebook structure, array size, and codebook size affect random beamforming performance in the near-field.

title: Simultaneous Direct and Indirect Channel Estimation for RIS-Assisted MIMO Communications
summary: This paper introduces an enhanced channel estimation method for reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications. Considering the presence of both the direct link from the base station (BS) to the user equipment (UE) and the indirect link \textit{via} the RIS, we formulate a tensor-based receiver for joint direct and indirect channel estimation called the TenDICE algorithm. The proposed receiver relies on an extended parallel factor analysis (PARAFAC) tensor model for the received pilot signals, from which the involved (direct and indirect link) channels are estimated using a simple alternating least squares scheme. The proposed TenDICE method is compared with the state-of-the-art least squares (LS) method, Khatri-Rao factorization (KRF) method, enhanced trilinear alternating least squares (E-TALS), and the theoretical Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB) based on normalized mean square error (NMSE) and spectral efficiency (SE). The proposed TenDICE outperforms the LS and E-TALS methods and performs similarly to the KRF methods while estimating the direct channel.

title: Low-Complexity Tensor-Based Channel Parameter Estimation for mmWave MIMO-Assisted Systems
summary: This paper presents a low-complexity tensor-based channel estimation framework for downlink mmWave massive MIMO systems using passive Butler-matrix beamforming. By modeling received signals as a third-order PARAFAC tensor, we exploit known pilot structures via bilinear alternating least-squares (BALS) optimization to reduce computational overhead. The decoupled spatial factors are then processed via 1D and 2D ESPRIT to extract angles of arrival and departure with automatic pairing. Additionally, we derive the Cramer--Rao lower bound (CRLB) for this architecture. Simulations confirm the proposed estimator outperforms conventional least-squares, achieving accurate channel reconstruction and approaching the CRLB at moderate-to-high signal-to-noise ratios.

title: Multistatic Terahertz ISAC for Object Shape Identification
comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables. Accepted to IEEE GLOBECOM 2026 Workshops (Third Workshop on Positioning and Sensing Over Wireless Networks)
summary: 6G networks are expected to sense their surroundings using the same waveforms that carry data. We ask how much can be learned about the shape of an object from the terahertz echoes that user equipment transmissions produce as they scatter from that object on their way to a ceiling-mounted access point, with no sensing hardware beyond the communication link itself. We build a physics-based multistatic forward model at a 300 GHz carrier with 50 GHz of bandwidth, combining Physical Optics (PO) and Physical Theory of Diffraction (PTD) scattering with an image-source multipath lattice, molecular absorption and directional horn antennas. The model makes explicit a property of the PO mechanism hierarchy that is usually left implicit. Six physically distinct mechanisms share only three frequency exponents, so the spectral slope does not by itself determine which mechanisms a target presents and therefore cannot by itself determine its geometry. Angular diversity is accordingly a requirement for identifiability rather than an optional refinement. We compare a transmitter-count-invariant 2D-CNN with a physics-informed RBF-SVM on object orientations never seen in training. Accuracy climbs from roughly 70 percent with one transmitter to 96-97 percent with 20. The CNN gains in two regimes, irregular placement and lossy targets, while on metal under quasi-uniform placement the SVM baseline is fully competitive. Performance falls off gradually under occlusion, holding 78 percent with three quarters of the surface hidden and 63 percent when the classifier has never seen an occluded target. Multi-object scenes are limited by interference between overlapping returns rather than by angular coverage, so presence detection saturates after roughly four transmitters.

title: Low-Complexity SVD-Based Precoding over Zero-Padded ISI Channels
summary: We propose a low-complexity SVD-based transceiver for zero-padded memory-$1$ ISI channels. Appending a single zero-padding symbol to an $n$-symbol block yields an $n\times(n-1)$ channel matrix with an \emph{exact symmetric tridiagonal Toeplitz Gram matrix}. This structure provides closed-form singular values and vectors, enabling exact SVD precoding and equalization via FFTs without explicitly forming dense SVD matrices. The resulting implementation has $O(n\log n)$ complexity and incurs only a $1/n$ rate penalty. The resulting parallel scalar subchannels enable joint adaptive PAM and power allocation for SER minimization, followed by exact soft-information computation for LDPC decoding. At comparable code rates near $0.945$, simulations show that our proposed scheme outperforms a conventional TX-FFE/RX-DFE system with hard-decision Reed-Solomon (RS) decoding by approximately $5$ dB at FER $10^{-5}$. At high SNR, it achieves nearly the same FER performance as a SOVA-based receiver with LDPC decoding, while replacing trellis-based detection with fast SVD precoding and exact scalar soft-output computation.

title: Generative Control of Time-Modulated Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces for Scalable Directional Modulation
summary: Time-modulated intelligent reflecting surfaces (TM-IRS) achieve directional modulation by switching their elements on and off at designed instants and durations, so that an undistorted signal reaches the intended user while appearing scrambled elsewhere. We propose a Flow Matching (FM)-based generative framework that designs these parameters for strong scrambling and reliable reception simultaneously. For orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) signals, we introduce a physics-informed reward that maximizes the time-modulation harmonic energy radiated in the null space of the legitimate-user response, subject to a minimum per-subcarrier signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), without requiring knowledge of adversary directions. Unlike prior generative flow network (GFlowNet) approaches, which assign discretized parameters sequentially, the FM model generates complete continuous configurations jointly, decoupling the generation depth from the number of elements and accelerating training. It also learns a distribution over configurations that can be resampled to vary the scrambling pattern. Numerical results show that, compared with a GFlowNet baseline, the proposed approach reduces the time to training loss near-saturation by $99.4\%$ on average for $3{\times}3$ to $12{\times}12$ surfaces, attains higher final rewards, scales to $80{\times}80$, and confines the low-symbol-error region more tightly around the legitimate user.

title: Beyond Hypercontractivity: Stronger Communication Converses via Rényi Contraction
summary: We study the relationship between strong data-processing inequalities for Rényi divergences and hypercontractivity. For Rényi divergences of order greater than one, we characterize the contraction of Rényi divergences through a property of the dual Markov operator that we name power contraction. Using the contraction coefficient, we derive an upper bound on rectangle probabilities in terms of their marginals that is at least as strong as the corresponding bound obtained via hypercontractivity. Combining this result with inversion of the binary Rényi divergence, we derive communication lower bounds for one-way communication-assisted agreement distillation. Examples involving binary symmetric and rare-event Z-channels illustrate the improvements over standard hypercontractive converses.

title: Self-Calibration DOA Estimation for Moving Dilated Arrays with Gain and Phase Errors
summary: Moving dilated arrays (MDAs) can increase the uniform degrees of freedom (uDOFs) while alleviating mutual coupling, but their performance is susceptible to unknown gain and phase errors (GPEs). To deal with this problem, we investigate self-calibration direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation for MDAs with unknown GPEs. First, multi-position observations are phase aligned to construct an equivalent virtual array with an enlarged aperture. Next, the motion-induced relationships among the GPEs are exploited to establish explicit calibration constraints. By leveraging the orthogonality between the steering vectors and the noise subspace, the joint estimation of the DOAs and GPEs is formulated as a constrained optimization problem. To solve this problem, a two-stage alternating optimization (AO) algorithm is developed. In the first stage, the GPEs are estimated in closed form with the DOAs fixed. In the second stage, the estimated GPEs are used to calibrate the covariance matrix, after which the DOAs are refined using the multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm. To obtain reliable initial estimates, a rotational invariance-like (RIL) initialization method is further developed by exploiting two translated virtual subarrays with identical GPEs. Furthermore, the Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) is derived to characterize the theoretical performance limit of the considered system. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method converges reliably and achieves accurate DOA estimation under different array apertures, numbers of snapshots, GPE levels, and numbers of sources.

title: A Ray-Traced Digital Twin for 5G NR Positioning with OpenAirInterface
comment: submitted at 22nd Wireless On-demand Network systems and Services Conference
summary: Evaluating 5G positioning on a physical testbed ties every measurement to one propagation environment and one antenna layout, so any question about an alternative deployment requires a new field campaign. We present a ray-traced digital twin of the GEO-5G testbed at EURECOM that drives an unmodified OpenAirInterface (OAI) 5G stack with per-antenna channels computed by Sionna-RT over a 3D model of the site. The distributed gNB antennas are modelled as independent radio devices rather than as elements of a compact array, which preserves the per-antenna absolute delays on which time-difference-of-arrival (TDoA) positioning depends. With them preserved, the twin drives OAI's SRS-based UL-TDoA pipeline to metre-level accuracy consistent with that reported for the physical deployment. We then use the twin to answer a question the physical testbed cannot. Widening the carrier truncates the tail of the horizontal error distribution without improving a typical position, and leaves the vertical error untouched, because the latter is limited by the array geometry rather than by the measurement. That limit is predictable from the antenna coordinates alone, and a height-diverse layout reduces the RMS height error by a factor of four.

title: Lightweight Time-Frequency Vibration Sensing for Consumer Device Condition Monitoring
comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, and 4 tables. Submitted to the 2027 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE 2027)
summary: Consumer rotating devices, including washing machines, air conditioners, electric fans, robotic vacuum cleaners, and home fitness equipment, increasingly rely on vibration sensing for intelligent condition monitoring and predictive maintenance. Ensuring reliable operation in these resource-constrained appliances requires efficient, lightweight artificial intelligence (AI) solutions capable of processing non-stationary signals under real-world operational interference. This paper proposes a lightweight AI-assisted vibration sensing framework that employs continuous wavelet transform (CWT) and Hilbert-Huang transform (HHT) to convert one-dimensional (1-D) vibration time-series signals into two-dimensional (2-D) time-frequency representations. These representations are subsequently analyzed using lightweight deep learning architectures, specifically MobileNetV3-Small, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and the You Only Look Once version 11 classification model (YOLOv11-cls). Public bearing benchmark datasets, including Case Western Reserve University (CWRU), Paderborn University (PU), and Intelligent Maintenance Systems (IMS), are utilized as representative rotating components to investigate model generalization. The proposed framework is designed with eventual embedded deployment in consumer electronics in mind. Experimental results demonstrate that CWT combined with YOLOv11-cls achieves high diagnostic accuracy, while MobileNetV3-Small provides an attractive low-latency alternative for computationally constrained edge platforms. Conventional random splitting is also compared with dataset-specific structured isolation. The results highlight the importance of avoiding data leakage and quantify tradeoffs in classification accuracy, parameter count, floating-point operations (FLOPs), model footprint, preprocessing cost, and central processing unit (CPU) inference latency.

title: Structure-Aware Online Optimization of the Age of Information with Unknown System Statistics
summary: Timely information dissemination is essential in modern communication systems, where low informational latency is critical for networked control, monitoring, and real-time decision-making. The Age of Information (AoI) has emerged as a fundamental metric for quantifying information freshness at the receiver. A key challenge in AoI optimization is selecting the update generation rate: infrequent updates lead to stale information, whereas overly frequent updates increase queueing delays. We develop a structure-aware, data-driven framework for adaptive AoI optimization modeled as single-server queues with unknown system statistics. Our key idea is to exploit analytical representations of the AoI gradient, which depend on a finite-dimensional collection of system quantities that can be estimated from observations collected during system operation. This reduces the online learning problem to estimating the quantities required by the gradient, rather than learning the AoI objective as a black box. We propose an online stochastic approximation algorithm that jointly estimates these quantities and optimizes the update generation rate. We prove almost sure convergence of the algorithm to the optimal update generation rate under mild regularity and moment conditions, despite the temporal dependence induced by the underlying queueing process. We demonstrate the framework in four representative incomplete-information settings, including FCFS queues with unknown service characteristics or hidden background traffic, a preemptive LCFS system with partial observations, and a generate-at-will system with threshold waiting.

title: Certified Outage Dimensioning of Fluid Antenna Receivers: Required SNR, Aperture, and Port Count
summary: We study the SNR, aperture, and port count needed to meet a target outage in a single-user downlink with a fixed transmit antenna and a single-RF fluid antenna receiver. For known spatially correlated Rayleigh channels and ideal port selection, a sampling-free residual certificate controls reduced-rank outage error over a continuous SNR interval. Positive Bessel features support large arrays, and bounded importance sampling converts the certificate into simultaneous design intervals. At 1 bit/s/Hz and outage $10^{-5}$, a four-wavelength, ten-port receiver requires 4.40--4.55 dB. Reducing its port count from 256 to ten costs 0.70--1.25 dB under a joint 95\% probability statement. At 3.5 wavelengths, ten ports require 4.90--5.05 dB. Integer-port screening across 3--8 dB shows how aperture and port requirements change with available SNR; an effective-SNR transformation extends these decisions to other rates. The reported intervals include model and sampling uncertainty under checked Gaussian covariance inputs. A constructive slow-growth rank bound and a 16--1024-port study support compact evaluation as port count grows.

title: Goal-Oriented Ordered Autoencoding for Successive Refinement in Progressive Communication
summary: Goal-oriented communication often struggles to sustain downstream task performance under variable and unpredictable bandwidth. We address this problem by proposing GO-OAE (Goal-Oriented Ordered AutoEncoding), which learns a progressively refinable quantized latent sequence, optimized directly for task utility rather than source reconstruction. Each component of the sequence is represented for transmission by its code index, and the learned ordering enables inference from any received prefix of the index sequence, with performance improving as more indices arrive. We prove that optimizing the goal-oriented distortion objective is equivalent to solving a weighted conditional information bottleneck formulation, and introduce an unbiased multi-prefix importance sampling (MPIS) estimator, to reduce GO-OAE training computational cost from O(BK) to O(Bm) with m << K, and reduces the estimator variance by a factor of 1/m. Experiments show that, on MiniImageNet, GO-OAE achieves over 96% of the lossless upper-bound classification accuracy using 324 bits per image (683X compression vs. raw RGB), and already attains over 94% of the upper bound with only 70% of the transmitted indices. It consistently outperforms reconstruction-optimized codecs and ordered autoencoders trained with uniform prefix sampling across all transmission budgets, demonstrating effective communication at extreme compression rates.

title: LLM-Assisted Hierarchical Interference Control for Satellite-Terrestrial Integrated Networks
summary: Time-varying aggregate interference from low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites challenges terrestrial-network (TN) protection, whereas conservative control degrades LEO quality of service (QoS). This letter proposes a hierarchical framework combining geometry-based interference estimation, QoS-constrained power control, adaptive energy detection, large language model (LLM)-assisted candidate ranking, stay-or-switch decisions, and target-band selection, with deterministic verification. The current band is retained only when both spectrum-hole and power-feasibility conditions hold, with periodic reevaluation. Over a 300-s horizon with 0.5-s sampling, the proposed method keeps the aggregate INR from exceeding the $-12.2$~dB threshold and achieves a time-averaged mean LEO-link rate of $320.97$~Mbps with $100\%$ QoS satisfaction. It markedly outperforms power-only and satellite-muting in jointly protecting the TN and preserving LEO QoS.

title: Gaussian BROJA Partial Information Decomposition in Closed Form
comment: 28 pages total, including 10 pages of main text, 2 main figures, 5 supplementary sections, and 5 supplementary figures
summary: The BROJA partial information decomposition provides an operationally motivated way to separate the information that two sources carry about a target into unique, redundant, and synergistic components. For continuous and high-dimensional variables, however, computing the BROJA decomposition requires solving a difficult optimization problem. Previous work showed that, when each source-target pair is jointly Gaussian, the problem can be reduced to finite-dimensional numerical optimization. Here, we derive a closed-form solution to this optimization problem, enabling direct computation of the BROJA decomposition in the general multivariate Gaussian setting. The resulting closed-form expression enables speedups exceeding two orders of magnitude for high-dimensional Gaussian BROJA PID. Code is available at https://github.com/brainsandmachines/Eigen_PID.

title: JEPA-kMMVAE: CSI Prediction for Time-Varying Wireless Channels
summary: This paper considers channel state information (CSI) prediction using neural networks for time-varying multi-antenna channels from noisy historical observations. The main challenge is to exploit temporal correlation while distinguishing channel evolution from observation noise. We propose JEPA-kMMVAE, which combines a joint-embedding predictive architecture with a k-memory Markov variational autoencoder to predict future CSI through temporally structured latent representations. The framework supports direct prediction and residual corrections relative to the latest latent state and noisy CSI observation. Simulation results show that the residual configuration outperforms the evaluated baselines at moderate and high input CSI signal-to-noise ratios, while sequence baselines remain more accurate under stronger noise.

title: Neural Polar Codes for Source Coding
summary: This paper presents a data-driven approach to lossless and lossy source compression using polar codes. Classical polar source coding achieves fundamental limits with low complexity for binary memoryless sources. However, for unknown q-ary sources with memory, successive-cancellation (SC) decoding requires an explicit source model and can be computationally prohibitive. We present analytical SC recursions and show that exact implementations scale quadratically with alphabet size and cubically with state-space size. To overcome these limitations, we develop neural polar decoders trained directly from data to approximate conditional distributions of synthetic polar coordinates without requiring an explicit source model. These learned distributions enable estimation of entropy rates, mutual information, and rate-distortion functions, and support explicit polar compression schemes. For lossless compression, we identify high-entropy polarized coordinates and reconstruct the remaining coordinates using the learned SC recursion. For lossy compression, we combine neural polar decoders with a neural test channel to estimate and optimize the mutual information-distortion tradeoff and construct an explicit lossy polar code. We also extend the framework to Wyner-Ziv compression with decoder side information by learning conditional polarized distributions and a reconstruction mapping. Experiments on memoryless sources, sources with memory, and real genomic data show that the learned decoders closely match analytical SC decoders when available and remain applicable when conventional methods are computationally infeasible or the source model is unavailable.

title: Towards Signal Processing In Networks: Multiplierless Block Transforms in Data Plane
comment: Submitted to the 2027 ICASSP-OJSP track, 9 pages, 4 figures
summary: In this paper, we propose a signal processing concept, signal processing in networks (SPIN), that executes signal processing tasks directly on programmable switches. Traditionally, signal processing tasks, such as denoising, decomposition, and dimensionality reduction, are performed on edge or cloud servers, i.e., raw streams are transmitted from sensors. This imposes a heavy processing load on edge/cloud servers and requires substantial bandwidth. SPIN addresses this problem by performing signal processing on the forwarding path. As an initial realization of SPIN, we implement a DCT-based block transform on a programmable switch. We redesign its computation using a lifting-based lattice structure, multiplierless approximation, and pipeline partitioning across stages in a programmable switch. We verify at the compiler level that the proposed implementation satisfies the strict hardware constraints of the Intel Tofino2--specifically regarding pipeline stages, packet header vector, and ternary content-addressable memory usage--and therefore enables line-rate processing. We further quantify the per-packet latency of the ingress match-action pipeline. The SPIN-oriented preprocessing adds 46 cycles (approximately 31 ns at 1.5 GHz). The total ingress match-action unit latency is approximately 87 ns, which remains consistent with the low-latency operation targeted by SPIN. Furthermore, we implement the proposed block transform on a BMv2 switch using P4 and evaluate it as preprocessing for in-network machine learning. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method improves classification performance over unfiltered baselines.

title: On Privacy Mechanism Design Under a Bounded $α$-Lift Leakage Constraint with $χ^2$-Utility
summary: We study the design of a statistical privacy mechanism under a bounded $α$-lift leakage constraint. An agent observes useful data $Y$, which is arbitrarily correlated with private data $X$, and releases $U$. The goal is to maximize Pearson $χ^2$-information $χ^2(Y;U)$ while satisfying the point-wise privacy constraint. This utility is an $f$-information that is nonnegative, obeys data processing, and measures the aggregate normalized change from the prior $P_Y$ to the posteriors $P_{Y|U=u}$. The main benefit of this choice is that $χ^2(Y;U)$ is exactly quadratic in the posterior perturbations; hence, no local approximation of the utility is required. For the nonlinear $α$-lift constraint, we derive a uniform Taylor-remainder bound that remains valid for the optimizing, $ε$-dependent perturbation. When $P_{X|Y}$ is invertible, this yields a closed-form quadratic surrogate, an explicitly scaled binary mechanism that satisfies the original $α$-lift constraint, a computable sufficient range for $ε$, and an $O(ε^{3/2})$ bound on the utility gap. For $α=2$, the solution is exact over an explicit range. We transfer these results to point-wise Rényi-divergence privacy, including an exact-feasible mechanism, an explicit privacy-budget range, and matching gap bounds. We also give an exact formulation for arbitrary leakage matrices and evaluate exact-feasible mechanisms numerically.

title: Scalable Quantum Clustering of Renewable Profiles via a Hybrid Qubit-efficient Strategy
summary: Large-scale renewable energy profile clustering is a computationally challenging NP-hard problem. Recent quantum computing techniques offer a potential remedy, yet their scalability is severely constrained by the limited qubit count of current quantum hardware. To address this issue, we first cast the problem into a QUBO form and then we propose a consensus-based variable reduction (CBVR) method to drastically cut qubit usage. More specifically, we tailor the one-hot constraint to eliminate assignment variables and leverage consensus analysis to convert stable clustering relations from initial anneals into equality constraints for further reduction. Experiments on real quantum hardware confirm that CBVR compresses oversized QUBO models into feasible sizes while retaining high clustering quality and efficiency.

title: Fundamental Limits of Covert queueing under Busy-Period Observations
summary: Consider a queueing system operated by Bob, which is intended to serve only jobs generated by a legitimate user, Willie. Willie's jobs arrive according to a Poisson process, and the service times are exponentially distributed. Bob seeks to covertly serve additional jobs arriving according to an independent Poisson process, without Willie detecting their presence. As the legitimate user, Willie is provided with certain statistics of each busy period by Bob. In particular, we consider two statistics: (i) the number of jobs served during each busy period and (ii) the duration of each busy period. We establish that, under either statistic, the maximum expected number of additional jobs that Bob can covertly serve obeys a square-root law. Specifically, over n busy periods, Bob can covertly serve additional jobs in the order of square root of n, whereas any scaling which is above square root of n enables Willie to asymptotically detect the presence of these additional jobs with vanishing error probability. Furthermore, we characterize the scaling constant associated with the square-root law, which we refer to as the covert queueing constant, for each of the two statistics. We compare the scaling constants corresponding to the two statistics and argue that the scaling constant under statistic (i) is no greater than that under statistic (ii).

title: ECGWmark: Deep Watermarking for Electrocardiogram Signals
summary: Secure transmission of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals remains a major challenge in telecardiology. While traditional mathematical watermarking can embed patient metadata directly into ECG signals, it is highly fragile against temporal desynchronization such as circular phase shifts. In contrast, existing deep watermarking approaches for temporal signals, such as audio, typically rely on lossy quantization, which compromises the high-frequency micro-morphological details critical for clinical diagnosis. To bridge this gap, we propose ECGWmark, a fully convolutional and quantization-free deep watermarking framework for medical time-series. ECGWmark operates in a continuous, full-resolution latent space and utilizes a localized frame-level mechanism to improve the robustness to severe desynchronization. Crucially, we introduce a differentiable Physiological Loss guided by a clinical classifier to preserve diagnostic semantics. Experiments on the benchmark MIT-BIH database show that ECGWmark maintains channel-bit extraction accuracy above 90% under the evaluated circular temporal shifts. Furthermore, under a rigorous inter-patient diagnostic evaluation, Class-V sensitivity changes from 71.97% to 76.50%, whereas Macro-F1 changes from 35.25% to 34.71% and Class-S sensitivity from 8.89% to 1.39%; these results indicate mixed class-level effects.

title: Heterogeneous Demand-Private Coded Caching: Exact Characterization for Two Users and Two Files
summary: We consider the demand-private coded caching problem with heterogeneous file sizes and cache capacities, where each user must recover its requested file without learning any information about the demands of the other users. We first extend the virtual-user reduction technique to accommodate heterogeneous cache sizes, thereby enabling the construction of demand-private coded caching schemes from non-private schemes. Our main contribution is an exact characterization of the memory-rate trade-off for the fundamental setting of two users and two files with arbitrary file sizes and cache capacities. Specifically, we characterize the optimal trade-off through eight linear inequalities and establish achievability by constructing explicit coded caching schemes for the non-trivial corner points, followed by memory sharing. These constructions include novel asymmetric cache placement strategies tailored to heterogeneous file sizes and cache capacities. For the converse, we exploit the distributional equivalences induced by demand privacy to derive information-theoretic lower bounds that explicitly account for the underlying heterogeneity. Our results generalize the exact memory-rate trade-off characterization for the homogeneous demand-private coded caching setting with two users and two files, while quantifying the additional transmission cost imposed by demand privacy compared with the non-private heterogeneous setting.

title: Tri-Hybrid SWIPT with Reconfigurable Parasitic Antennas
summary: We propose a coupling-aware tri-hybrid precoding architecture for simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) using reconfigurable parasitic antennas. By integrating multiport network theory and information theory, we develop a third precoding layer that explicitly accounts for mutual coupling and reactive energy storage within the antenna domain. To efficiently optimize this architecture, we propose a low-complexity tri-hybrid solution comprising coordinate descent (CD) for parasitic reactive load optimization, a singular value decomposition (SVD)-based analog precoder, and a protective partial zero-forcing (PPZF) digital precoder. Numerical results demonstrate that the transmit array introduces impedance mismatch that reduces the real power accepted by the antenna array. Moreover, the proposed tri-hybrid architecture significantly outperforms hybrid precoding by constructively exploiting the coupling effects, yielding substantial gains in spectral efficiency (SE) and sum non-linear harvested energy (NLHE) at a fraction of the hardware cost.

title: One Thing Leads to Another: The Essentials of Time Series Causal Discovery
comment: 16 pages, 3 figures, accepted for publication in the IEEE Signal Processing Magazine
summary: Time series causal discovery --- the process of detecting causation between time series --- has its roots in signal processing research from over a half century ago. It has since received active and widespread interest, evolving into different forms across domains such as statistics, dynamical systems and machine learning. Entering this fragmented and constantly evolving research landscape can be daunting. This tutorial provides a unified overview of time series causal discovery across research communities. We introduce the key principles invoked by modern discovery methods, and we discuss their limitations and assumptions. We also discuss how discovery methods are evaluated, benchmarked and fine-tuned. We further discuss how causal discovery for time series is becoming crucial for downstream tasks in agriculture and Earth science, in healthcare, and in artificial intelligence systems. We believe that this tutorial will serve as a valuable resource in navigating the deluge of recent causality research, as well as an invitation to signal processing audiences to contribute to causal problems. To further help readers, we host a companion repository to link to useful code packages and resources at https://github.com/CHAI-UK/Awesome-Time-Series-Causal-Discovery.

title: JEPA-kMMVAE: CSI Prediction for Time-Varying Wireless Channels
summary: This paper considers channel state information (CSI) prediction using neural networks for time-varying multi-antenna channels from noisy historical observations. The main challenge is to exploit temporal correlation while distinguishing channel evolution from observation noise. title: CNN-Transformer with Sigmoid Label for High-Resolution Sub-Degree DOA Estimation
summary: This paper addresses the grid quantization error of deep-learning (DL)-based direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation. Classification- based DOA methods discretize the continuous angular space into a grid, so that with a peak-based read-out, the accuracy and resolution are limited by the grid step and by the width of the label peak. To address this issue, we propose a sigmoid label that encodes the sources' DOAs as the sum of angle-shifted monotonic sigmoid functions. Differentiating the output of a CNN-Transformer network trained with the sigmoid label produces sharp spectral peaks at the source DOAs. Combined with a moderately refined grid step of 0.25 degrees, the CNN-Transformer with the proposed sigmoid label attains sub-degree accuracy and a 1-degree resolution, breaking the limit of the grid quantization error. Under the unified CNN-Transformer backbone, we compare the proposed Sigmoid label with the Gaussian label, the 0-1 hard label, and the binary cross-entropy (BCE) baseline. Numerical results demonstrate that the Sigmoid label attains the highest accuracy and superior resolution compared to other labels.

title: Tri-Hybrid SWIPT with Reconfigurable Parasitic Antennas
summary: We propose a coupling-aware tri-hybrid precoding architecture for simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) using reconfigurable parasitic antennas. By integrating multiport network theory and information theory, we develop a third precoding layer that explicitly accounts for mutual coupling and reactive energy storage within the antenna domain. To efficiently optimize this architecture, we propose a low-complexity tri-hybrid solution comprising coordinate descent (CD) for parasitic reactive load optimization, a singular value decomposition (SVD)-based analog precoder, and a protective partial zero-forcing (PPZF) digital precoder. Numerical results demonstrate that the transmit array introduces impedance mismatch that reduces the real power accepted by the antenna array. Moreover, the proposed tri-hybrid architecture significantly outperforms hybrid precoding by constructively exploiting the coupling effects, yielding substantial gains in spectral efficiency (SE) and sum non-linear harvested energy (NLHE) at a fraction of the hardware cost.

title: Blind and Asynchronous Initial Beam Acquisition and Clock-Assisted Re-Acquisition in Standalone Mobile MIMO-OFDM Systems
summary: Building upon our preliminary study, this paper proposes a standalone beam-management framework for mobile MIMO-OFDM systems that integrates Blind Initial Beam Acquisition (BIBA) with Clock-Assisted Re-Acquisition (CARA). BIBA is a blind and asynchronous protocol that requires neither prior synchronization nor an out-of-band feedback channel, so the Base Station (BS) and User Equipment (UE) can independently identify the beam pair maximizing received signal strength. To handle subsequent link drops, the newly introduced CARA protocol exploits the clock synchronization established after BIBA to reduce the re-acquisition time by approximately 55% compared with BIBA. The operational reliability of both protocols is bounded by a probabilistic feasibility analysis under random UE mobility trajectories. Protocols are validated on a 28 GHz mmWave testbed under practical hardware constraints, including beam-switching and Time Division Duplex (TDD) latencies, and measured Software-Defined Radio (SDR) software processing delays. Finally, we formulate a unified Finite State Machine (FSM) model for both BIBA and CARA to ensure robust integration into practical wireless systems

title: Suppressing Multiple GNSS Interferers with Local-Gradient Adaptive Notch Filtering
summary: Adaptive notch filters (ANFs) based on the normalized least mean squares (NLMS) algorithm are an established technique for suppressing narrowband interference in GNSS receivers. The traditional solution for multiple interferers is simply cascading the NLMS-ANF into multiple stages but this solution degrades performance when multiple chirp jammers of similar power are present. We propose a low-complexity modification to the cascaded NLMS-ANF update rule to resolve this: a local gradient (LG) formulation: LG-ANF. The LG-ANF forms a locally bandlimited gradient signal by translating the input to baseband around the current frequency estimate, low-pass filtering it, and translating it back, thereby attenuating competing interferers before adaptation. The modification generalizes the traditional NLMS-ANF to handle the similar-power multiple interferer problem, using just one additional parameter. We characterize the gradient-averaging failure analytically and visually, demonstrate independent chirp tracking in the worst-case two-chirp scenarios, and evaluate statistical suppression performance by sweeping amplitude ratio against a standard NLMS-ANF, a frequency-locked-loop (FLL)-based ANF and a per-sample oracle upper bound. We further characterize the LG advantage over various ANF parameters and chirp conditions. Simulations show that the LG-ANF reduces to the standard NLMS-ANF outside the pathological multi-chirp regime, while recovering up to 4dB of in-band suppression around pathological amplitude ratios under per-condition optimization of the local bandwidth, and up to 13dB for selected edge-case parameter combinations. These optimized results represent an upper bound on the achievable LG gain. In a hardware experiment using a fixed alpha_lp=0.5, the LG-ANF extends position-lock survival by 24s relative to the standard ANF.

title: HF Single-Station Localization via Multimode Ray Tracing and Time-Frequency Information Fusion
summary: High-frequency (HF) single-station localization estimates an emitter location from measured directions of arrival (DOAs) and an ionospheric propagation model. When the propagation mode composition cannot be identified from conventional direction-finding (DF) measurements, the same DF observation may produce multiple physically valid ground landing points under different propagation modes, making the location inversion ambiguous. This paper proposes a multimode time-frequency information fusion localization method (MTFIF-L).Rather than assuming a propagation mode a priori, MTFIF-L retains valid landing points generated under different propagation modes and uses repeated observations across time windows and, when available, multiple operating frequencies to progressively constrain the resulting candidate locations. Experiments on four measured HF links examine the respective roles of multimode candidate retention, cross-window processing, and cross-frequency processing. All four links yield unique location decisions. Links A--C achieve relative errors of $1.40\%$, $0.78\%$, and $3.41\%$, respectively.Link D, the only single-frequency case, also yields a unique decision from repeated temporal observations, although its post- localization error is substantially larger. Propagation-path analysis further reveals link-dependent differences in reflection layer, hop count, magnetoionic mode, and elevation angle among the ray-tracing paths associated with the measured links.Overall, the results show that repeated temporal observations can support localization within an individual frequency, while multifrequency information provides additional robustness against unreliable frequency-specific outcomes, enabling HF single-station localization under unknown and potentially coexisting propagation modes while retaining interpretable propagation information for post-localization analysis.

title: OpenH-RF: A Large-Scale Ultrasound Raw Channel Dataset Initiative
comment: Preprint: 15 pages, 15 figures, 3 tables. Dataset (v1.0): https://open-h.github.io/OpenH-RF
summary: Medical ultrasound is a widely accessible, real-time imaging modality, yet progress in data-driven ultrasound research is constrained by the scarcity of large, open collections of raw channel data. Existing public datasets are predominantly based on reconstructed images, while the smaller number of open raw channel datasets is generally specialized to individual reconstruction or imaging tasks, limiting the development of general-purpose methods and foundation models that operate directly on ultrasound signals. While interpretive tasks can be performed on reconstructed images, many of the key technical challenges in ultrasound imaging, such as aberration correction and reverberation reduction, require the raw channel data itself. We introduce OpenH-RF, a community-driven open dataset initiative comprising approximately 40 TB of medical ultrasound raw channel data in 19,332 acquisitions, contributed by 38 institutions across academia and industry, spanning in-vivo, phantom, and simulated data. Each dataset is annotated with a number of supported tasks, ranging from generalized reconstruction, speed-of-sound estimation, and aberration correction to blood flow imaging, motion estimation, quantitative ultrasound, and image interpretation. OpenH-RF provides a unified, self-contained data format that captures raw channel data together with the acquisition, probe, metadata, and reconstruction information required for reproducible processing across scanners and acquisition schemes. The corpus is publicly hosted under a permissive CC BY 4.0 license and can be streamed programmatically and selectively at scale. By bringing heterogeneous ultrasound data into a common representation, backed by modern data infrastructure, OpenH-RF lowers the barrier to working with raw channel data and aims to open medical ultrasound research to new communities. See https://open-h.github.io/OpenH-RF.
